about.title: Half Moon Bay Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Half Moon Bay draws visitors and locals alike to its coastline, farm stands, and small businesses lining SR-1 and San Mateo Road — but a slick entryway, broken stair, or poorly lit parking lot can turn a simple outing into an injury. California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you. That's why what happens right after your fall matters: photos of the spot, names of witnesses, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage can make a real difference later. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured people in Half Moon Bay with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your fall, explain your options, and handle the claim on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. If you're unsure whether your fall qualifies, a quick conversation costs nothing and starts the clock on preserving evidence before it disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney knows how to gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Getting a preservation letter out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so any share of blame assigned to you can lower what you recover. A skilled advocate works to keep the focus on the hazard and the owner's failure to address it.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Half Moon Bay?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property is owned by a public entity — like a city building or park — the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to talk to an attorney as soon as possible to know exactly where you stand.

items.question: What if I fell at a business near Rt 1 or SR-1 without seeing an employee nearby?
items.answer: You don't need an employee to have witnessed the fall for a claim to have merit. What matters is whether the hazard existed long enough that the owner should have caught it during reasonable inspections. Photos, timestamps, and any nearby cameras can help establish that timeline.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to get help?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money. There's no cost to have your fall evaluated.
